sections.title: Sound of ics
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (ics) /iks/. Its main sound is heard in the word (xilofono) /ksiˈlɔfono/, which means xylophone. The letter makes two sounds in Italian. Both sounds are consonant clusters, where two consonants sit together without a vowel between them. You find this letter in loanwords and learned words.

sections.title: How to say ics
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to block the air. Release it sharply, then slide your tongue tip behind your upper teeth to hiss. Keep your voice off. For the second sound, make the same block and hiss, but keep your voice on. Touch your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Spelling of ics
paragraphs: In most borrowed words and learned terms, you pronounce two voiceless consonants. You hear this sound in (extra) /ˈɛkstra/ and (taxi) /ˈtaksi/. Between vowels in some French borrowings, the sound becomes voiced. You can hear this voiced cluster in (ex) /ˈɛɡz/.

sections.title: Comparing ics
paragraphs: Do not turn the start of this letter into a single hiss like English xylophone. Keep both consonants clearly heard, as in the middle of box. Do not drop the first sound. When the letter is voiced, say both consonants smoothly without a pause, just like in the English word eggs.
